page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-8 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 30 GB of RAM, equating to 3.75 GB of memory per core. It runs on an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware allocation is dedicated, providing 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and int8 operations. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2203.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 34.68 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, reaching the top 10% with a Geekbench text processing score of 3031.0. Multi-core and memory benchmarks generally align with the middle 50% of tested instances, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 8381.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 8425.22. Memory bandwidth reaches 668.72 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drops to 61.17 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

While the instance demonstrates average performance in database operations and static web serving, it exhibits limitations in complex machine learning tasks. Specifically, LLM text generation using a medium 7B model is weak, yielding only 7.18 tokens/sec. However, prompt processing for the same model is average at 56.94 tokens/sec. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core capabilities, this instance is suited for general-purpose computing, software compilation, text processing, and moderate web serving workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 30 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs but features advanced CPU instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. In benchmark testing, it demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%, and text processing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. However, resource-intensive tasks like medium-sized LLM text generation show weaker performance. This instance is suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, and general-purpose web serving where dedicated CPU resources are required without the need for local storage.
